Application Materials.content:
**Documents and information you’ll need**
- a copy of your degree certificate and transcript, or a partial transcript if you’re still studying
- contact details for two academic references
- a personal statement
- an up-to-date CV
- your approved English Language test* (if applicable)
- a letter of sponsorship, if you need one.
* Applicants who have not yet completed an [approved English language test](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/masters/doc/english-language-requirements-2) may apply for a Masters course prior to taking a test.

Interview Requirements.content: Interviews do not form part of the Business School’s standard admissions process. However, in some cases, an applicant may be invited for an interview if it will help inform whether an offer should be made.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **A bachelor degree with a 2:1 (hons) in any subject.**
- Quantitative skills are beneficial but not essential; **a willingness to engage with quantitative materials is required.**
- **International qualifications:** The University accepts a range of [international equivalent qualifications](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/masters/doc/international-equivalents-2).
- **Applicants from China:** accepted postgraduate qualifications include **4 year Bachelor degrees**. The University of Leeds uses institutional lists when assessing applications from accepted Chinese institutions, and requirements may vary by school. If the course asks for **2.1**, applicants need **70%-85%, depending on your institution**.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
English language requirements: **IELTS 6.5 overall, with no less than 6.0 in any component**. For other English qualifications, read [English language equivalent qualifications](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/international-admissions/doc/entry-requirements "English language equivalent qualifications").
International students who do not meet the English language requirements for this programme may be able to study a postgraduate pre-sessional English course, designed with a progression route to the degree programme. Options include [Language for Business (6 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/k022/language-for-business-6-weeks- "Language for Marketing 6 weeks") and [Language for Business (10 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/k023/language-for-business-10-weeks- "Language for Business: Marketing (10 weeks)"), as well as [six week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j615/online-academic-english-presessional-6-weeks-) and [10 week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j614/online-academic-english-presessional-10-weeks-). Longer postgraduate pre-sessional English courses are also available.
Application documents include your **approved English Language test** (if applicable). Applicants who have not yet completed an [approved English language test](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/masters/doc/english-language-requirements-2) may apply for a Masters course prior to taking a test.

Program Overview.content:
Start date: September 2026. Delivery type: On campus. Duration: 12 Months (Full time).
**Understand the people behind the data as you unlock crucial insights businesses need to grow.** Brands are constantly looking to make smarter, more meaningful connections with consumers, so customer data has never been more important. With a strong focus on understanding the numbers behind human behaviour, this course gives you both advanced analytical skills and strategic marketing know-how. Learn skills spanning big data, predictive analytics and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and stand out with this unique Masters. From retail, location planning, logistics and marketing, your options are open to forge the path you want to take next. Plus, you'll be based in Leeds, a city that’s right at the heart of global marketing action.
Why study at Leeds:
- **Give yourself the edge in a competitive job market:** Gain sought-after skills in analytical expertise and psychological insight.
- **A course with dual focus:** With input from Leeds University Business School and the School of Geography, this means you’ll be connecting complex analytics directly to market outcomes.
- **Affiliation with the UK’s [Consumer Data Research Centre](https://www.cdrc.ac.uk/):** Make the most of our connections as well as the expertise of the School of Geography’s [Centre for Spatial Analysis and Policy](https://environment.leeds.ac.uk/geography-research-centre-spatial-analysis-policy).
- **Close industry connections:** Connect you to emerging trends in topics including consumer behaviour, decision science and digital and interactive marketing.
- **Access a wealth of data and resources:** When it comes to data sciences, our campus-based [Leeds Institute for Data Analytics](https://lida.leeds.ac.uk/) is the place to be.
- **State-of-the-art computing facilities:** You can immerse yourself in coding, programming and modelling software.
- **Join Leeds Data Society:** You can join societies that link in with your studies which regularly hosts guest speakers from other organisations.
- **International Study Tour:** Apply for a place on a week-long [international study tour](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/masters/doc/international-study-tour-2) which includes company visits, guest lectures and networking events.
Leeds University Business School has triple accreditation from the three leading bodies, AACSB, AMBA and EQUIS.
Core modules will introduce you to a range of analytical methods, ensuring you develop a solid foundation in the essential skills for consumer analytics and marketing strategy. You’ll learn how to analyse geographic data using GIS software, developing your knowledge of retail modelling to evaluate new markets and locations. You’ll study consumer and business analytics, while learning how to deploy data to inform decisions about marketing strategy. You’ll also be involved in collaborative work to analyse data and make marketing predictions. The choice of one optional module allows you to develop your marketing or geography interests, explore new ideas and concepts, or develop skills and knowledge relevant to your career path. The course culminates in a final dissertation, allowing you to demonstrate the knowledge and skills you’ve gained through detailed analysis of a specific topic. Two options are available – you can complete a standard research dissertation, with either a Marketing or Geography academic focus, or choose to complete a practice-based dissertation, allowing you to work on a real-world marketing problem.
You’ll be taught using a range of methods including lectures, tutorials, seminars and workshops. On this course, you’ll be taught by expert academics, from lecturers through to professors. You may also be taught by industry professionals with years of experience, as well as trained postgraduate researchers.
Where this degree could take you:
- Job roles some consumer analytics and marketing strategy graduates have obtained include Marketing Data Analyst, Junior CRM Manager, Retail Store Manager on leadership programmes, and Graduate Marketing Executive.
- Typical organisations graduates work with include retail and FMCG, marketing and advertising agencies, e-commerce and digital platforms, consultancy and market research, hospitality, tourism and leisure, and technology and data services.
- Graduates who aspire to a research or academic career will also be prepared for a [research degree](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/research-degrees) in marketing.
The Global Industry Programme gives Masters students a great opportunity to gain real-world experience through live industry projects. This course offers you the chance to spend time abroad, usually as an extra academic year, which will extend your studies by 12 months; once completed, you'll be awarded the ‘international’ variant in your degree title. A work placement can be undertaken as an industrial placement year as part of your course; if you decide to undertake a placement year, your period of study will be extended by 12 months, and on successful completion, you'll be awarded the ‘industrial’ variant in your degree title.

Curriculum.content:
Start date: September 2026. Delivery type: On campus. Duration: 12 Months (Full time).
Core modules introduce analytical methods and a foundation in consumer analytics and marketing strategy, including GIS software, retail modelling, consumer and business analytics, and using data to inform marketing strategy. Modules include marketing strategy, marketing analytics and consumer behaviour. Students also complete collaborative work to analyse data and make marketing predictions. One optional module allows students to develop marketing or geography interests. The course culminates in a final dissertation; students can complete a standard research dissertation, with either a Marketing or Geography academic focus, or a practice-based dissertation working on a real-world marketing problem.
[For more information and a full list of typical modules available on this course, please read Consumer Analytics and Marketing Strategy MSc in the course catalogue](https://catalogue.leeds.ac.uk/Programme/202627?code=MSC-BS%2FCAMS)

Teaching methods include lectures, tutorials, seminars and workshops, with the rest of the time spent in independent learning. Assessment may include formal exams, group projects, reports, computer simulation exercises, essays and written assignments, group and individual presentations and reflective logs.
The course offers the chance to spend time abroad, usually as an extra academic year, extending studies by 12 months. After successful completion, students are awarded the ‘international’ variant in the degree title.
Students may undertake an industrial placement year as part of the course; if undertaken, the period of study is extended by 12 months. On successful completion of the placement year, students are awarded the ‘industrial’ variant in the degree title. Work placements are not guaranteed.

Cost of Attendance.content:
The information is provided as a guideline only, based on average spending. The following tables are estimates for a single student in 2025 based on the latest data available. The actual amount will depend on your accommodation type and availability, and your lifestyle. They don’t include tuition fees.
| Cost category | Estimated cost per week |
| --- | --- |
| University accommodation, self-catered | £117 to £265 |
| University accommodation, catered | £205 to £273 |
| Private accommodation, self-catered | £110 to £300 (costs may be more for higher specifications) |
| Groceries: food, toiletries and cleaning products | £31 to £38 |
| Household bills: gas and/or electricity, water and broadband internet (these are included in most university accommodation and some private accommodation) | £14 to £17 |
| Personal costs: transport, socialising, restaurants/takeaways, clothes and mobile phone | £44 to £68 |
**Estimated total budget per week: approximately £199 to £423**

Financial Aid.content:
Global Community Bursary
- **Value**: £10,000 to support maintenance, paid in instalments
- **Who is eligible**: Particularly deserving international applicants (including EU) from low income countries or low income households in under-represented countries applying for a Business School Masters programme* for 2026 entry.
- **Deadline**: **21 June 2026, 23:59pm (BST)**
You will be automatically considered for a Business School Global Community Bursary when your application for your [Masters course](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/masters/doc/courses-2) is reviewed. Those selected will progress to the final stage and will be invited to complete an application asking for more details of how you are financing your studies, your household circumstances and your aims and ambitions relating to your course choice.
To be considered for the bursary you must:
- be classified as an international student for fee purposes
- have applied for an eligible Business Masters programme* for 2026/27 before **21 June 2026** and be holding an offer
- come from a low-income country or from a lower-income household in a country underrepresented at the Business School
- demonstrate an excellent academic track record, and be predicted to achieve or have achieved a Bachelors degree with a 2:1 (hons) or equivalent
- show how your background and life experiences have encouraged you to make an impact on your community
- demonstrate how Masters study at the Business School will help you achieve your short and long-term career objectives
- not hold any other scholarship or bursary contributing to the cost of living. The award may be held in conjunction with any scholarships supporting fees only.
The bursary is conditional on meeting all offer conditions, being granted a visa and registering for the course initially applied for academic year 2026/27. Awards will not be deferred if holders cannot commence their studies in 2026/27. Awards will not be extended should a student need to extend their studies beyond the standard 12-month study period.
Applicants will be notified of the status of their application by **5 July 2026**. Number of scholarships available: 30.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: Please note that we do not permit deferrals.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
A conditional offer from the University of Leeds means you need to achieve the grades or points outlined in your offer letter. Your offer letter will also explain any English language requirements, if applicable. If you have an academic offer condition, the University may need to see your degree certificate and transcripts as evidence. If you have an English language condition, you may be able to meet the requirements by taking a [pre-sessional course at the Language Centre](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/language-centre/doc/postgraduate-pre-sessional-english). You can upload evidence that you have met your conditions and accept your offer in the [application portal](https://myleedsportal.leeds.ac.uk/signin-landing/). You may have to accept your offer again if it becomes unconditional.
If your offer has an academic condition, you will need to include official translations alongside your final academic documents if they were not originally produced in English.
If you take a [pre-sessional English course](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/language-centre/doc/postgraduate-pre-sessional-english) with the Language Centre to meet your language condition, you may be eligible for a combined offer. This means that when you pass your pre-sessional, and have met any conditions in your offer letter, you are automatically enrolled on your degree course.
